1.why: Text is a clean sans-serif with comfortable line spacing and short lines, but letter spacing looks default rather than expanded and the font is not an identifiably dyslexia-friendly typeface.

2.why: All headings, buttons, and messages use sentence case with no italics, no all-caps blocks, and no dense paragraphs on any of the six screens.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow column with full-width controls and large tap targets, so it reads cleanly at phone width.

4.why: Every instruction is one short plain sentence, e.g. 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

5.why: The verification field shows the placeholder 'Example: 123456' and the email field shows 'name@example.com', modelling the expected input format.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a couple of short sentences; the longest text anywhere is the single-line log block.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears on any screen; the only code entry ('123456') is typed by hand and no authenticator-secret or backup-code screen with copy support is shown.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered anywhere; the flow never advances past 'Step 2 of 4' to authenticator setup.

9.why: Login uses standard native email/password inputs that password managers can usually fill, but nothing observable demonstrates autofill support for the verification code field.

10.why: A persistent 'Step X of 4' banner marks progress and actions are large high-contrast buttons, though on the code screens the leftover solid-blue 'Send code' button with its focus ring competes with 'Check code'.

11.why: From the code-entry screen onward the user sees two full-width solid-blue buttons ('Send code' and 'Check code') plus 'Send a new code', so more than one main-styled action is presented at once.

12.why: Status banners plainly state each result and what comes next: 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: The user can retry 'Check code' and re-request via 'Send a new code' with no penalty or lockout messaging, and the entered code stays visible, though no reveal/hide toggle exists.

14.why: The error banner 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' states the problem and two concrete fixes without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or session timer appears on any screen, and the wording 'Enter it when you are ready' explicitly removes time pressure.
